report:
Conclusion: **Supported, with scope limits.** In postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high fracture risk, daily subcutaneous abaloparatide for 18 months reduced new vertebral fractures versus placebo in the phase 3 ACTIVE trial: about **0.58% vs 4.22%**, relative risk ~0.14 (≈86% relative reduction), with nonvertebral fractures also lower. FDA labeling reflects this high-risk postmenopausal indication, and follow-on data suggest benefit is maintained when abaloparatide is followed by alendronate. A later meta-analysis likewise concludes abaloparatide lowers vertebral-fracture risk and raises BMD. This does **not** mean it is appropriate for every postmenopausal woman; it is generally reserved for high/very-high fracture risk or failure/intolerance of other therapy, with treatment duration and safety limits considered by clinicians.
